summary: Karin Meyers works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She studied under Jay L. Garfield and served at Kathmandu University as an assistant professor and director of the MA program in Buddhist studies at the Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

Karin Preisendanz is an Indologist and philosopher. She held positions at the University of Hamburg from circa 1993 to 1996 and served as Professor Dr. at the University of Vienna from circa 1996 to 2023.

Karl Brugmann was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Georg Curtius circa 1868–1871. He held posts at the University of Freiburg (circa 1884–1887) and Leipzig University (circa 1887–1919), where he succeeded Curtius.

Karl Brunnhölzl works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied under traditional teachers including Khenpo Tsültrim Gyamtso Rinpoche, Tenga Rinpoche, Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche, Sangye Nyenpa Rinpoche, Ringu Tulku, and Lama Thubten.

Karl Debreczeny is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. He completed his PhD at the University of Chicago under doctoral supervisor Wu Hung and teacher Jenny Purtle, and served as curator at the Rubin Museum of Art (attested 2008).

Karl Ferdinand Johansson was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Uppsala University in 1880. He served as University Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology of Indo-European Languages at Uppsala University from circa 1893 to 1925.

Karl Florenz was a scholar of Japanology, Indology, and linguistics. He held a professorship at the University of Tokyo from circa 1889 to 1914 and later held a post at the University of Hamburg from circa 1914 to 1934.

Karl Friedrich Geldner was an Indologist, Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar, and linguist. He studied at Tübingen and Leipzig, and held posts at Tübingen, Halle-Wittenberg, Humboldt University of Berlin, and the University of Marburg (1907).

Karl H. Potter was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Harvard University in 1955. He served as a professor at the University of Minnesota (circa 1956–1970) and at the University of Washington (attested 1987–1999).

Karl Hoffmann was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held posts at Saarland University from circa 1952 to 1955 and as professor at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg from circa 1955 to 1983.

Karl Jettmar was an Indologist, archaeologist/historian, and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He held academic posts at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz from circa 1961 to 1964 and at Heidelberg University from circa 1964 to 1983.

Karl Rosenkranz was a philosopher who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin, Heidelberg University, and the University of Halle-Wittenberg between circa 1824 and 1828. He later held a post at the University of Halle-Wittenberg from circa 1830 to 1833.
Karl Verner was a linguist who studied at Aarhus Katedralskole. He held an academic post at the University of Copenhagen from circa 1883 until 1896.

Karl-Heinz Brodbeck is a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1970–1980), later serving there, at the Ifo Institute, and as professor at FHWS and the Munich School of Politics and Public Policy.

Karma Lekshe Tsomo is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who earned a doctorate at the University of Hawaii (~1990–2000). She held posts at the University of San Diego (~2000) and the University of California, San Diego (attested 2013).

Karma Phuntsho is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He earned his PhD at the University of Oxford (Balliol College) under Michael Aris and David Seyfort Ruegg, later holding a postdoctoral post at CNRS (circa 2003–2005).

Karma Sonam Palmo works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. She completed Shastri and Acharya degrees at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, followed by a PhD at the University of Tasmania under Lucy Tatman and Sonam Thakchoe.

Karma Ura is a Tibetologist who earned an undergraduate degree at Magdalen College, Oxford (~1983–1986) and a graduate degree at the University of Edinburgh (~1989–1990). He became Director of the Centre for Bhutan Studies circa 1999.

Karuna Kusalasaya was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He served as a research scholar and Assistant to the Director at Visva-Bharati University and as Professor of Sanskrit at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University.

Karunesh Shukla is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. Attested in 1991, he served as Professor and Head of the Department of Sanskrit and Prakrit Languages at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University and founded the Nagarjuna Buddhist Foundation.
